advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the runbook Verify grep with the documented error signature (`EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused`) instead of `'Cannot email'`.
evidence: Documented signature elsewhere: infra/runbooks/gerrit-outbound-mail.md ~L14 `com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused`

search across repo shows `Cannot email` appears ONLY on the grep line — nothing else in the runbook or config uses that phrase, so the verify string is inconsistent with the failure the runbook is counting.
advisory.finding: The runbook's Verify step greps error_log for `'Cannot email'`, but every other part of the runbook (and the gerrit.config comment) identifies the failure signature as `EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused`. `Cannot email` will not match that documented signature, so the operator's before/after count will not reflect the errors the runbook describes, breaking the 'Count unchanged = fixed' verification.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the verify grep to match the documented signature, e.g. `grep -c 'Mail Error: Connection refused' /var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log` (or confirm and use the exact outer log prefix Gerrit emits).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the runbook verify grep to match the documented error signature ('Mail Error: Connection refused' / 'EmailException'), not 'Cannot email'.
evidence: Documented error signature (same runbook): "com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused"
gerrit.config comment: "`EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused` — 4,119 of them"
advisory.finding: The runbook's verify command greps for 'Cannot email' but the documented error signature (established repeatedly in the same runbook and in gerrit.config) is 'Mail Error: Connection refused' / 'EmailException'. The grep string will not match the errors described, so the verification step reports zero even when the failure persists.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the verify command to grep for the actually-logged signature, e.g. `grep -c 'Mail Error: Connection refused' /var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add infra/compose/gerrit.config to config-check.sh check 1 (git-config parse validation) so a malformed [sendemail]/other section fails CI before reaching main.
evidence: config-check.sh:31-36 loops only over `infra/gerrit/project.config infra/gerrit/replication.config` for `git config -f "$f" --list` validation
config-check.sh:3-4 states its purpose: 'validate every infra config so a MALFORMED config can never reach `main`'
The diff edits infra/compose/gerrit.config (adds a `[sendemail]` git-config section, gerrit.config:106-122), and compose-up.sh:142 copies that exact file into the live site etc dir

ABSENCE: no test or config-check branch parses infra/compose/gerrit.config as git-config (search for `compose/gerrit.config` finds only the autodeploy trigger, the runbook, and the signal test — none validate its syntax)
advisory.finding: The newly-added `[sendemail]` section in infra/compose/gerrit.config is not covered by any parse-validity gate: config-check.sh check 1 parses only infra/gerrit/project.config and infra/gerrit/replication.config, not infra/compose/gerrit.config — so a git-config syntax error in the new section would reach main undetected and only surface at Gerrit injector-creation on the live gate.
advisory.suggested_fix: In config-check.sh:32 add `infra/compose/gerrit.config` to the loop list: `for f in infra/gerrit/project.config infra/gerrit/replication.config infra/compose/gerrit.config; do`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop or strengthen the detail-string assertion in the gerrit.config signal test — it checks static prose, not that gerrit.config was the path that triggered the config_manual signal.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:190 emits a fixed string: `err config_manual "infra config changed in $TARGET — replication/g2p/refs-meta/gerrit.config need a MANUAL operator apply ..."` — the word 'gerrit.config' is present unconditionally, independent of the detected path

The regression this diff introduces is genuinely caught by the two primary assertions (signal emitted at line 114 + reason==config_manual at line 120), which fail RED-first if gerrit.config is removed from CONFIG_PATHS
advisory.finding: The `"gerrit.config" in payload['detail']` assertion verifies a hardcoded prose string rather than the triggering path: autodeploy.sh:190 statically embeds the literal word 'gerrit.config' in the config_manual detail regardless of which CONFIG_PATH actually changed, so this assertion would still pass if a different config file (e.g. project.config) were the sole trigger.
